items.claim: Karnataka's own tax revenue was Rs 9,042.7 crore in 2000-01, according to RBI's Handbook of Statistics on State Government Finances (2004).
items.note: 2000-01 is the 5th column of the 1996-97 to 2003-04 block. The last two columns are RE/BE, so 2000-01 is an accounts figure, but the page does not label it 'Accounts'. Search results say RBI's revenue-receipts appendix (PublicationsView id=12350) shows 9,04,267 lakh, but I did not open that page. Nominal rupees, not adjusted for inflation.

items.claim: Karnataka's own tax revenue is budgeted at Rs 2,20,000 crore for 2026-27. It was Rs 1,93,100 crore in 2025-26 (revised estimate) and Rs 1,77,447 crore in 2024-25 (actuals).
items.note: The 2025-26 RE is Rs 15,000 crore below its own BE. Nominal comparison: 2,20,000 / 9,042.7 is about 24 times, which is plain arithmetic, not inflation-adjusted. A per-person figure was not computed because no official 2026 population count exists (Census 2027 is pending); see gaps.

items.claim: From 15 June 2024 the Congress government raised the Karnataka Sales Tax on petrol from 25.92% to 29.84% and on diesel from 14.3% to 18.4%. In Bengaluru petrol went from Rs 99.84 to Rs 102.86 a litre and diesel from Rs 85.93 to Rs 88.94.
items.quote: Karnataka Sales Tax (KST) has been raised from 25.92 percent to 29.84 percent on petrol and from 14.3 percent to 18.4 percent on diesel
items.note: The article's summary says 18.44% for diesel. The April 2025 notification also cites 18.44% as the old rate.

items.claim: From 1 April 2025 the sales tax on diesel was raised again, from 18.44% to 21.17%, which put diesel at about Rs 91.02 a litre.
items.quote: the Karnataka Sales Tax rate on diesel has been revised from 18.44 percent to 21.17 percent
items.note: Search results point to the official notification at gst.kar.nic.in/latestupdates/dieselnotification2425.pdf, which I did not open.

items.claim: From 5 January 2025 the state cabinet raised bus fares by 15% across KSRTC, NWKRTC, KKRTC and BMTC. BMTC fares had last been revised in January 2015.
items.quote: decided to increase the bus fares in the state-owned transport corporations by 15 per cent
items.note: PTI copy. Free travel for women under Shakti continued.

items.claim: From 5 November 2026 Karnataka raised bus fares again: by about 23% on KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC, and by 32-35% on BMTC. BMTC's minimum fare went from Rs 6 to Rs 10.
items.quote: will increase by 23 percent to 35 percent from 5 November
items.note: Corroborated by ThePrint/PTI, 4 Nov 2026 (https://theprint.in/india/karnataka-hikes-bus-fares-not-to-make-profit-but-to-save-corporations-says-minister/3090229/): KSRTC '23 per cent on average', BMTC '33-35 per cent'. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh cited diesel costs and losses.

items.claim: From 9 February 2025 the maximum Namma Metro fare in Bengaluru rose from Rs 60 to Rs 90, on the recommendation of a Fare Fixation Committee.
items.govt: BMRCL, a joint venture of the Centre and the state. The fare panel was headed by retired Justice R. Tharani and included a Union ministry official and a former Karnataka official.
items.quote: the maximum fare increased from Rs 60 to Rs 90
items.note: Do not attribute this solely to the state government. After protests BMRCL partly revised the fares (Deccan Herald reported the steepest hikes capped at 71.43%; not opened). South First (6 Feb 2026) reports a further revision from 9 Feb 2026 'capped at five percent', but the new fare slabs were not confirmed.

items.claim: Nandini milk went up by Rs 3 a litre from 1 August 2023 (toned milk from Rs 39 to Rs 42).
items.quote: The Karnataka cabinet has decided to hike price of Nandini milk by Rs three per litre from August 1.

items.claim: From 26 June 2024, Nandini milk packets cost Rs 2 more but contained 50 ml more milk (1 litre at Rs 42 became 1,050 ml at Rs 44).
items.quote: the price of each packet is being increased by Rs 2 with an additional 50 ml of milk
items.note: The government said this was not a per-litre price increase. Present it as Rs 2 more per packet for 50 ml more milk. The extra 50 ml was withdrawn on 1 April 2025.

items.claim: Nandini milk went up by Rs 4 a litre from 1 April 2025 (toned milk from Rs 42 to Rs 46).
items.quote: Milk prices in Karnataka will increase by Rs 4 per litre starting April 1
items.note: PTI copy. Some outlets give Rs 44 to Rs 48, which looks like a different variant. Use the PTI toned-milk figures.

items.claim: Nandini milk went up by Rs 8 a litre from 1 November 2026 (toned milk from Rs 46 to Rs 54). Rs 7 of the increase goes to farmers.
items.quote: Consumers will pay ₹8 more per litre for Nandini milk supplied by the Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF) from November 1
items.note: Corroborated by OneIndia, 29 Oct 2026 (https://www.oneindia.com/bengaluru/nandini-milk-price-hike-in-karnataka-rs-8-per-litre-increase-from-november-1-farmers-to-get-rs-7-e-8245307.html). OneIndia does not give the toned-milk retail price; that comes only from South First. Search results said the curd hike was partly cut back by Rs 2 a litre on 2 Nov 2026; not opened.

items.claim: Electricity consumers have paid an extra 36 paise per unit since 1 April 2025, after KERC allowed the power supply companies to recover the government's share of employee pension and gratuity costs.
items.govt: Ordered by KERC (the regulator) during the Congress (Siddaramaiah) government. The government said it was KERC's decision.
items.quote: will have to pay an additional 36 paise per unit starting from April 1 as a surcharge
items.note: The same tariff order cut energy charges by 10 paise per unit and raised fixed charges by Rs 25 for 2025-26 (TNM, 2 Apr 2025). Gruha Jyothi free-power users are reportedly shielded; the government bears the cost.

items.claim: Property guidance values, on which stamp duty is charged, were raised by 25-30% on average from 1 October 2023. They had not been revised for five years.
items.govt: Congress (Siddaramaiah); announced by Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda
items.quote: On the whole, the revised guidance value will increase by 25 to 30 per cent on an average.
items.note: The increase varied by area.

items.claim: From 31 August 2025 the property registration fee was doubled from 1% to 2% of property value. Stamp duty stayed at 5%.
items.quote: increased property registration fees from 1 percent to 2 percent, which will come into effect from 31 August
items.note: Reported all-in cost rose from 6.6% to 7.6%; some outlets say 7.5%.

items.claim: Under the BJP government, the 2020-21 budget raised the tax on petrol from 32% to 35% and on diesel from 21% to 24%, effective 1 April 2020. Petrol went up Rs 1.60 a litre and diesel Rs 1.59.
items.quote: The CM proposed to increase the rate of tax on petrol from 32% to 35% and diesel from 21% to 24%.

items.claim: On 4 November 2021 the BJP government cut fuel prices by Rs 7 a litre, which it said would cost the exchequer Rs 2,100 crore. This followed the Centre's excise duty cut.
items.quote: the Karnataka government announced reduction on the prices of both fuels by additional Rs 7 per litre
items.note: Included for balance: this was a cut, not a rise. Search results put the new rates at 25.9% (petrol) and 14.34% (diesel), but I did not open a page stating them. That is the base the June 2024 increase started from.

items.claim: Under the BJP government, Nandini milk and curd went up by Rs 2 a litre from 24 November 2022 (toned milk to Rs 39).
items.quote: announced an increase by Rs 2 the prices of Nandini brand of milk (per litre)
items.note: The effective date of 24 Nov is inferred from 'Thursday'. Search results said an earlier Rs 3 KMF proposal was rolled back after CM Bommai intervened, but I did not open a page confirming it.

items.claim: Enrolment in Karnataka's government schools has fallen by 17 lakh over the past 15 years, the School Education Minister told the Assembly in December 2025.
items.as_of: 11 Dec 2025 (written reply in the Assembly, Belagavi)
items.govt: Congress (minister Madhu Bangarappa); the 15-year span covers both Congress and BJP governments
items.quote: Enrolment in government-run schools in Karnataka has dropped by 17 lakh over the past 15 years
items.note: This is the government's own figure, but the start and end numbers and years are not given. Medium confidence because no base year is stated.

items.claim: D.K. Shivakumar was sworn in as Karnataka Chief Minister on 3 June 2026 at Lok Bhavan, Bengaluru. Siddaramaiah had resigned on 28 May, and the Congress Legislature Party elected Shivakumar its leader on 30 May.
items.quote: The leadership transition follows Shivakumar's election as the leader of the Congress Legislature Party on May 30.
items.note: All India Radio (newsonair.gov.in, 3 Jun 2026) confirms Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot administered the oath. G. Parameshwara became Deputy CM. Outlets disagree on whether he is the 18th, 25th or 34th CM, so avoid the ordinal.

items.claim: In his 2023 election affidavit (Kanakapura), Shivakumar declared total assets of Rs 1,413.80 crore and liabilities of Rs 503.07 crore, including family members' assets.
items.govt: n/a (he was a candidate and KPCC president)
items.note: This is a declared figure, not a valuation. Our reading of the MyNeta page gives liabilities of Rs 503 crore, while ADR/Tribune coverage of the 2026 CM report cites Rs 265 crore; this is unresolved, so do not use a liabilities number on air.

items.claim: In his 2018 affidavit, Shivakumar's family assets were put at Rs 840 crore. His declared wealth rose 68% by 2023.
items.quote: in the 2018 affidavit, the combined value of the property held by his kin was pegged at Rs 840 crores
items.note: ANI copy on ThePrint. Search results say ADR's 2018 ministers report gives Rs 840.01 crore (not opened). Some 2018 reports gave Rs 600 crore or 730 crore depending on whose assets were counted, so say 'family assets of Rs 840 crore'.

items.claim: ADR's July 2026 analysis of all 31 sitting Chief Ministers names D.K. Shivakumar the richest, with declared assets of about Rs 1,413 crore, ahead of Andhra Pradesh's N. Chandrababu Naidu at Rs 931 crore.
items.as_of: ADR/National Election Watch report released 27 Jul 2026
items.quote: with Congress’ DK Shivakumar of Karnataka emerging as the richest among them with assets valued at Rs 1,413 crore
items.note: The Tribune article (Aditi Tandon) is republished on ADR's site. ThePrint (30 Jul 2026, also on adrindia.org/node/99811) says 'Shivakumar is the richest CM, with declared assets totalling over Rs 1413 crore.' This is ADR's finding based on self-declared affidavits, so we do not need to frame it as our own comparison.

items.claim: The CBI registered a disproportionate-assets case in October 2020 under consent given by the BJP government in September 2019. It alleges Shivakumar acquired Rs 74.93 crore in assets beyond his known income between 2013 and 2018, while he was a minister.
items.govt: Consent given under BJP (Yediyurappa); withdrawn under Congress (Siddaramaiah)
items.quote: The CBI alleged that Shivakumar amassed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income between 2013 and 2018
items.note: This is an allegation; there is no conviction or court finding of guilt. The Rs 74.93 crore figure comes from the Tribune report of 29 Aug 2024 (next item).

items.claim: On 23 November 2023 the Congress cabinet withdrew consent for the CBI probe. On 26 December 2023 it referred the Rs 74.93 crore case to the Lokayukta. On 29 August 2024 the Karnataka High Court dismissed the CBI's challenge as non-maintainable. The CBI and BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal have appealed to the Supreme Court, where a bench led by Justice Surya Kant was assigned the case in September 2025.
items.quote: the Rs 74.93 crore disproportionate assets case against Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar to the Lokayukta for investigation
items.note: Separately, on 15 July 2024 the Supreme Court dismissed Shivakumar's own plea to quash the CBI FIR (LiveLaw, https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/supreme-court-dk-shivakumar-plea-for-quashing-cbi-disproportionate-assets-case-263370). I found no 2026 ruling. As of the latest report found, the appeals were pending and the Lokayukta probe had no reported outcome.

items.claim: In a letter sent to the Prime Minister's Office on 6 July 2021, the Karnataka State Contractors Association, led by president D. Kempanna, alleged that contractors were being made to pay commissions of up to 40% on government tenders. The state was then governed by the BJP.
items.govt: BJP (B.S. Yediyurappa when the letter was sent; Basavaraj Bommai from 28 Jul 2021)
items.quote: How do they expect contractors to work well if we have to give up 40 per cent of our tender money?
items.note: Allegation only. CM Bommai called the letter generic and without proof.

items.claim: Justice H.N. Nagamohan Das's inquiry, covering works from 26 July 2019 to 31 March 2023, submitted a report of about 20,000 pages to CM Siddaramaiah in March 2025. It found no evidence of a systematic 40% commission, but did find lapses and irregularities in tendering. It named two former BJP MLAs and one engineer as facing specific contractor complaints.
items.as_of: Report submitted March 2025 (South First says 13 March); article 3 Apr 2025
items.govt: Panel set up by the Congress government to probe the BJP-era allegation
items.quote: The allegation of 40 percent commissions is not 100 percent true
items.note: The panel also said the problem was not confined to one party. Named people (G.H. Thippareddy, Roopali Naik, engineer S.F. Patil) are subjects of contractors' allegations, not proven guilty. Do not name them on air without that framing. Star of Mysore (16 Mar 2025) confirms the report was submitted and its scope.

items.claim: On 11 April 2025 the Karnataka cabinet decided to set up a Special Investigation Team, with a two-month deadline, to pursue the Nagamohan Das report.
items.quote: decided to constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to gather more details
items.note: The cabinet date is inferred from 'Friday' and the article date. Search results show a later study committee under retired IAS officer Sudhir Krishna to examine the report, but I could not open that article (Deccan Herald returned 403). No SIT outcome was found.

items.claim: In a letter to CM Siddaramaiah dated 25 September 2025, the Karnataka State Contractors Association, led by president R. Manjunath, alleged that the commission demanded had doubled under the Congress government. It also demanded release of about Rs 32,000 crore in pending bills.
items.quote: the percentage of commission demanded has now doubled under your government
items.note: Organiser is RSS-affiliated. A neutral PTI version exists (newsdrum.in, deccanherald 3745090) but returned 403. The 2026 items from ThePrint and Hans India repeat the same claim. This is an allegation only; no percentage was proven.

items.claim: On 13 February 2026, R. Manjunath, president of the Karnataka State Contractors Association, told reporters in Madikeri that commission demands for clearing bills had roughly doubled under the Congress government compared with the BJP.
items.quote: But now, the situation is worse than before.
items.note: Allegation. The Hans India said the government had not officially responded.

items.claim: On 30 September 2026, R. Manjunath, president of the Karnataka State Contractors Association, alleged that the commission demanded to clear dues is higher than under the previous BJP government, and said about Rs 38,000 crore in bills was pending. CM Shivakumar replied that they should file an affidavit naming who has to be paid, and said he would have it investigated.
items.quote: It is more compared to the previous period.
items.note: PTI. Manjunath declined to give a percentage. Shivakumar also blamed the BJP government for approving works without budget provision. Allegation only.

items.claim: In August 2023 a BBMP contractors' body told the Governor that 10-15% commission was being demanded on behalf of the Bengaluru Development Minister (then D.K. Shivakumar). Within days the association's president said it had made no allegation against him.
items.quote: We have not made any allegation against Deputy Chief Minister Shivakumar.
items.note: Use only with the retraction. State Contractors Association president D. Kempanna also said 'No minister has asked for a commission.'

items.claim: No court or Lokayukta has found that a 40% commission, or any specific commission rate, was paid under either government. The judicial inquiry found the 40% figure not proven, and the contractors' later claims about the Congress government remain allegations.
items.quote: The allegation of 40 percent commissions is not 100 percent true
items.note: This finding is that no ruling turned up in searches, not proof that none exists. The Nagamohan Das panel was a commission of inquiry, not a court.

gaps: Per-person tax burden: not computed. The 2001 Census population is available, but 2026 has only official projections, and Census 2027 results are not out. Under the no-estimates rule we skipped it.
The 2000-01 own-tax figure is nominal. No inflation-adjusted comparison was sourced, so do not imply a real 24-fold increase.
Namma Metro: the exact fares after the partial rollback (late Feb 2025) and the Feb 2026 revision (capped at 5%) were not confirmed.

Electricity: no consolidated net per-unit change for 2023-2026 was found. KERC's FY24 tariff change (ordered around the 2023 change of government) was not verified. Neither was the final multi-year tariff for 2026-27 (fixed charge reported as +Rs 30).
BWSSB water tariff increase (2025) and excise/liquor duty increases were not verified with amounts.

Fuel: no 2026 change in state sales tax was found. The new rates after the Nov 2021 cut (25.9% petrol, 14.34% diesel) appear only in search snippets; the Udayavani and Business Standard pages returned 403.
Nov 2022 milk: the rollback of a Rs 3 proposal after CM Bommai intervened appears only in snippets.
Status of the Nagamohan Das SIT and the Sudhir Krishna study committee: no outcome found. The Deccan Herald pages returned 403.
The DA case at the Supreme Court: no 2026 hearing outcome found. The latest dated item is from 22 Sep 2025.
Shivakumar's 2023 liabilities: MyNeta shows Rs 503 crore, while the ADR 2026 coverage reportedly cites Rs 265 crore. Unresolved.
A3: no well-sourced NSS/NHA out-of-pocket health spending or teacher/doctor vacancy series for Karnataka since 2000 was verified. The enrolment claim has no base-year figures.
The neutral PTI copy of the Sept 2025 contractors' letter (newsdrum/Deccan Herald) returned 403; the only opened source is Organiser.
